transcript: The other night, I saw Goddess at The Public, a new musical inspired by the myth of Marimba, goddess of music. In this story, she takes on a human form as a singer in an Afro-jazz club in Mombasa, Kenya, entrancing everyone around her including a young man named Omari who has just returned home. Omari is caught between the precise pathway in politics which his family has laid out for him, and his own passions for music and social change. With music at the forefront of this story, we get stunning performances, vibrant production numbers, and the thrills of a live band in an authentic club-like setting. In a way, this show is a cross between some other contemporary musicals — some stylistic and thematic elements invoke those of Hell's Kitchen, Buena Vista Social Club, and Hadestown, but in the context of Kenya and Afrobeats. I found the actual plot to be pretty thin, but the theme of music as an almighty power and a source of healing and unity is evident in these characters and the incredible performances. Witnessing Amber Iman’s leading performance live is crazy, and she's definitely giving one of the most captivating vocal performances I've experienced in awhile. Her voice is so incredibly rich and pretty unmatched on a technical level. There were moments where I didn't even register what she was singing about because I was just taken by how incredible her vocals were. It's rather fitting that her character is of the mythical and the supernatural, considering how otherworldly her talent is. If you're looking for a new, original musical with an emphasis on the music part, Goddess was just extended at The Public and will be running through June 8th. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
